# Cinematic story template — the long-form documentary standard

A packaged workflow and house style for a **narrated, chaptered product film** built
from MotionScenes: a measured local voice, a chaptered beat plan, cinematic scenes
that always move, a real caption track, and one assembly pass into the open
project. The reference is the 5:00 OpenCut Reinforced documentary built in project
`11`: 37 beats, 12 chapters, 65 narration lines, 191 caption cues, 30 fps.

This is the long-form sibling of `templates/video-pipeline/` (the 59 s showcase).
Same renderer, same kit, different film: the showcase sells a moment, this template
carries an argument for five minutes. Read `STYLE.md` for the grammar, this file
for the process.

## What it packages

| Piece | Where | What it fixes |
|---|---|---|
| House defaults | `defaults/video.config.json` | tempo, gaps, caption look, chunk rules, bed level |
| Scaffold | `scripts/new-video.mjs` | `videos/<slug>/` with the documentary shape |
| Narration | `scripts/narration.mjs` | local TTS at 1.6, measured placement, fit check, markers |
| Subtitle re-chunk | `scripts/build-captions.mjs` | 12 words / 72 chars / 900 ms cues from measured audio |
| Beat → scene | `scripts/build-scenes.mjs` | windows derived from the voice, one scene per beat |
| Parallel render | `scripts/render.mjs` | files only, three workers, never races the project |
| Assembly | `scripts/assemble.mjs` | tracks, voice, bed, scenes, captions, chapter markers |
| Re-style captions | `scripts/style-captions.mjs` | the 100-clip `set-text` window, solved |
| Drawing kit | `lib/kit.mjs` | palette, primitives, camera, particles, waveforms |
| UI kit | `lib/ui.mjs` | window, viewer, bin, inspector, timeline, playhead |
| Composers | `lib/composers.mjs` + `lib/scenes/*.mjs` | 38 reference beats in eight chapters |
| Beat chooser | `beats/beat-library.json` | what each composer is for |
| Review gates | `CHECKLIST.md` | frame, chapter, caption, voice, duration, honesty |
| Reference film | `videos/example-story/` | the 5:00 script and beat map |

## The house style, in numbers

| | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Voice | from **Settings → Narration** (reference: Ngọc Huyền, VieNeu-TTS local) | never hardcode a voice name; `script.voice` overrides for one film |
| Tempo | **1.6** | the house reading speed; 1.0 sounds like an audiobook |
| Gaps | **190 ms** between lines | a breath, not a pause |
| Speaking rate | **≈28 characters/second** at 1.6 | measured, used by the fit check; recalibrate per voice |
| Line length | 25–45 words, 3.5–5.5 s | one idea per line |
| Film length | measured voice + 1.4 s tail, or an exact `duration_ms` | a documentary is as long as its argument |
| Speech coverage | **90–96 %** of runtime | unlike the showcase, the voice carries the film |
| Beats | 4–13 s, 25–40 per five minutes | a beat is one idea |
| Chapters | 12 numbered markers in 5:00; a chapter lasts as long as its argument (7–50 s) | the marker is a promise, not a metronome |
| Captions | Be Vietnam Pro 25 pt, bottom, −280 bp, `#F4F6FA` on `#0B0D11` @120, pad 8000 | fixed under a moving camera |
| Cue rules | ≤12 words, ≤72 chars, ≥900 ms, +110 ms lead | two to three cards per spoken line |
| Music | 120 bpm, **constant −6 dB**, no per-sentence ducking | a bed, not a ducking demo |
| Frame | 1920×1080, 30 fps | whole-second cuts land on the 0.5 s beat grid |

## The six steps

Run from the workspace root (the folder with `project.json` and `tools/or`).
`$V` is the video folder, `$T` is this template's folder.

```sh
node $T/scripts/new-video.mjs --slug my-film --title "My film" --seconds 300

# 1. Write the words and the chapter plan. One line per idea, 25–45 words.
$EDITOR videos/my-film/script.json videos/my-film/video.config.json

# 2. Speak the script at 1.6 and measure it. Needs the local TTS server running.
node $T/scripts/narration.mjs --video videos/my-film --attach project.json --json

# 3. Re-chunk the measured audio into documentary cues.
node $T/scripts/build-captions.mjs --video videos/my-film

# 4. Build the bed: 120 bpm, then bake it to −6 dB (clip volume is app-only).
node tools/music.mjs --out work/music/bed.wav \
  --prompt "cinematic documentary, warm, 120 bpm, light drums" --json
ffmpeg -y -v error -i work/music/bed.wav -filter:a "volume=-6dB" \
  -ac 2 -ar 48000 work/music/bed-minus6.wav

# 5. Beat windows → scenes → rendered clips. Three workers is the sweet spot.
node $T/scripts/build-scenes.mjs --video videos/my-film
node $T/scripts/render.mjs --video videos/my-film --workers 3 --attach project.json

# 6. Import everything into the open project, review, then save.
node $T/scripts/assemble.mjs --video videos/my-film --attach project.json --dry-run
node $T/scripts/assemble.mjs --video videos/my-film --attach project.json
tools/or project save --attach project.json --json
```

`assemble.mjs` creates the tracks it needs, clears the ones it owns, imports the
SRT as a real caption track, styles every cue, and refreshes the chapter markers.
`--dry-run` prints the plan without touching the project.

## Config shape

```jsonc
{
  "slug": "my-film",
  "title": "My film",
  "tempo": 1.6,                       // narration time-stretch; 1.6 is the house tempo
  "gap_ms": 190,                      // breath between lines
  "tail_ms": 1400,                    // film ends this long after the last measured line
  "duration_ms": 300000,              // optional: pin an exact runtime instead
  "canvas": { "width": 1920, "height": 1080 },
  "narration": { "chars_per_second": 28 },   // measured rate at this tempo
  "captions": {
    "anchor": "bottom", "sizePt": 25, "offsetY": -280, "weight": "medium",
    "font": "be-vietnam-pro", "color": "#F4F6FA",
    "background": "#0B0D11", "backgroundPadding": 8000, "backgroundOpacity": 120,
    "chunk": { "max_words": 12, "max_chars": 72, "min_cue_ms": 900, "lead_ms": 110 }
  },
  "music": { "file": "work/music/bed-minus6.wav", "duckDb": null, "levelDb": -6 },
  "beats": [
    { "id": "open", "composer": "coldOpen", "start_ms": 0, "lines": ["mo1", "mo2"] },
    { "id": "editor", "composer": "editorBuild", "lines": ["ui1", "ui2"] },
    { "id": "close", "composer": "close", "lines": ["ket1"] }
  ]
}
```

* `lines` are `script.json` ids. A line's `start_ms` is where its voice sits. Set
  `start_ms` on a chapter opener; leave it off elsewhere and the voice places the
  line end to end. The beat window is derived from its lines, so **do not
  hand-write `end_ms`** — the film's length comes from the voice, or from
  `duration_ms`.
* `composer` is a key in `beats/beat-library.json`. A beat without a composer the
  kit knows is refused, not silently skipped.
* `duckDb: null` is deliberate. A documentary keeps a constant bed under the
  voice; ducking is for a showcase with big music beats. Set a negative number
  only when the bed is an event, not a floor.

## The reference arc (12 chapters, 5:00)

| Window | Chapter marker | Beats | What carries it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0:00.5–25.6 | 01 · Mở | coldOpen, layerFlow, layersAlign | a shot becomes four layers, the layers become a timeline |
| 25.6–34.1 | 02 · OpenCut Reinforced | reveal | the product is named once |
| 34.1–68.0 | 03 · Dựng phim | editorBuild, editActions, cutRipple, previewExport | the real editor, exact-frame edits, a deliverable |
| 68.0–117.7 | 04 · Chat Assistant | assistantScope, assistantRole, chatAsk, acpBridge, harnessRail, chatResult | the assistant reads the project; ACP keeps keys on the near side |
| 117.7–142.4 | 05 · Motion Scene | motionCode, motionBuild, motionMorph, motionTimeline | code becomes geometry, geometry becomes a clip |
| 142.4–170.1 | 06 · Giọng đọc local | ttsScript, ttsWave, whisperListen, whisperCues | local voice, local transcript, reviewed captions |
| 170.1–179.9 | 07 · Quy trình khép kín | workflowLoop | the loop closes on one machine |
| 179.9–208.0 | 08 · Miễn phí và sở hữu | mitDoc, localCost, ownership | what free means, what still costs, who owns the files |
| 208.0–233.3 | 09 · Thực tế và giới hạn | reality, releaseCard, platformGap | the honest limits of this release |
| 233.3–254.7 | 10 · Bài toán mobile | mobileQuestion, providerTrap, notarize | the mobile gap and the install reality |
| 254.7–261.8 | 11 · Cộng đồng | community | the invitation |
| 261.8–300.0 | 12 · Cùng xây | contribPath, checks, commitment, close | how to contribute, what is checked, the end card |

Vary the viewpoint between beats: wide shot, user view, close-up, inside-view.
Two dense UI beats in a row is a fail even if both are polished.

## The subtitle method

Captions are a **real caption track**, never baked into the scene. The method has
three parts:

1. **Timing from the measured audio, not the text.** `narration.mjs` speaks and
   stretches each line, then records `start_ms`, `end_ms` and `duration_ms`.
   `build-captions.mjs` re-chunks the *caption text* over that measured interval.
   No model, no transcription, no TTS call in the re-chunk step.
2. **Readable cards, never leading the voice.** At most 12 words / 72 characters,
   at least 900 ms on screen, later chunks start 110 ms after their character
   position, and no cue may overlap the next. The reference film averages 9 words
   and 1.4 s per cue — 191 cues for 65 lines.
3. **One styled layer.** `assemble.mjs` imports the SRT and runs `timeline
   set-text` on every cue: bottom anchor, 25 pt, −280 bp, Be Vietnam Pro,
   `#F4F6FA`, `#0B0D11` at 120 alpha, 8000 milli-point padding. Because
   `set-text` only searches the first 100 clips, the styling runs in windows of
   96 on a temporary caption track and moves the spill back. The finished project
   has one caption track with every cue styled.

## Rules the template enforces

* **The windows tile the film.** Every beat is non-empty, the first starts at 0,
  each starts where the previous ended, the last ends at the film length.
* **No line is silently cut.** A line under 80 % of its expected duration is
  re-spoken sentence by sentence and stitched.
* **A line that overruns its space is reported.** `narration.mjs` prints the
  slack; fix the wording, never speed the voice up to fit.
* **Every chapter is a marker.** Markers are rebuilt from the script's `marker`
  fields, so the timeline outline and the film agree.
* **Renders are revision-safe.** `render.mjs` writes files only; every project
  write happens later, sequentially, in `assemble.mjs`.
* **Every frame moves.** A composer animates a camera over the whole beat and
  keeps two or three secondary motions running.

## Pitfalls that cost time

* **`timeline set-text` searches 100 clips.** A five-minute film has ~190 cues.
  Style 96 at a time on a temporary caption track, then move them back (both
  `assemble.mjs` and `style-captions.mjs` do this).
* **A media item caches the duration it was imported with.** Re-rendering a file
  in place keeps the old length; remove the media item when a render's length
  changes.
* **`insert-clip --duration` must not exceed the media duration.** Floor to
  milliseconds.
* **Keep rationals reduced** (`591/500`, not `1182000/1000000`).
* **Node ids are unique across a whole scene.** Prefix every piece (`imSun`,
  `auWave`, `c1`); a duplicate id fails validation.
* **Scene text lives inside a 5 % margin.** Keep type at 14 px or larger and
  lines short; everything readable stays above `SAFE_BOTTOM`.
* **Camera zoom stays 0.94–1.5** except for a deliberate dive; the backdrop is
  oversized so a zoom never shows the canvas edge.
* **Render and assemble are separate steps.** Editing the project while renders
  run causes revision conflicts.
* **Three parallel workers** is the sweet spot; more adds contention.
* **The TTS server must be running** at the endpoint in `narration-settings.json`.
  The voice name comes from Settings → Narration; `script.voice` is the one-film
  override.
* **Clip volume is app-only.** Bake the −6 dB bed into the file with ffmpeg; the
  CLI has no gain verb.

## A worked example

`videos/example-story/` is the reference film's script and beat map: 65 lines,
37 beats, 12 chapters, 5:00. It expects `work/music/bed-minus6.wav` (step 4) and
runs the six steps unchanged. The script leaves `voice` empty on purpose — the
reference machine's voice was Ngọc Huyền; on another machine the measured timing
shifts, and `build-scenes.mjs` will say so until `duration_ms` is adjusted.

## Provenance

Built from project `11` in the OR workspace: 37 MotionScene beats, 65 narration
lines at tempo 1.6 with 190 ms gaps (285.9 s spoken), 191 caption cues on one
track, a 120 bpm bed at a constant −6 dB, 12 chapter markers, 30 fps, 1920×1080.
The kit, the UI primitives and the 38 composers are those beats with the
project-specific narration removed.

# Style — the cinematic documentary grammar

The look and the rhythm this template packages, stated as rules a composer and a
script can be judged against. The reference is the 5:00 OpenCut Reinforced film in
project `11`. Read this before writing a beat or a line; read `README.md` for the
process.

## 1. The frame

* 1920×1080, 30 fps. The sequence rate is set once; every rendered beat is
  `duration × 30` frames exactly.
* The palette is five flat colours, not a gradient: near-black ground
  (`#08090B`), panel (`#111317`), edge (`#2A2F37`), ink (`#EDF0F5`), and one
  accent per chapter (amber `#F4B64E`, cyan `#4FD1C5`, blue `#6094E8`, violet
  `#A78BFA`). A sixth colour is a decision, not a default.
* `SAFE_BOTTOM = 900` in `kit.mjs`. Everything readable lives above it; the
  caption band sits under it. A shape may cross the line, a word may not.
* The backdrop is oversized and the camera never exposes a canvas edge. Zoom
  stays 0.94–1.5 except for a deliberate dive.

## 2. Camera grammar

Every beat has one camera move over its whole length, not a push at the cut.

* **Wide** — establish a world or a workspace. Slow drift, 1.0–1.1.
* **User view** — the frame is the app window; the camera settles, then tracks a
  cursor or a playhead.
* **Close-up** — one control, one word, one waveform. 1.2–1.4.
* **Inside view** — the camera enters the thing it was looking at (a viewer, a
  scene, a code pane). A dive is a handoff, not decoration: it carries the cut.
* **Return** — pull back to the wide for the chapter close, or hand off directly
  to the next beat's first frame. Never end on an empty frame.

Vary the viewpoint between consecutive beats. Two UI beats in a row is a fail
even when both are polished.

## 3. Beat anatomy

A beat is 4–13 s and carries exactly one idea. In the first 0.8 s the idea is
visible before any text explains it. Through the middle, two or three secondary
motions keep running (particles following a beam, a waveform tightening, a clip
landing where the cursor pointed). At the end, the beat hands off: a match cut, a
fold, a wipe, a dive.

Content must **change form**, not merely appear: a line becomes geometry, a clip
becomes a layer, a code line becomes a shape, a layer becomes a timeline. A title
card, a paragraph, or a diagram that replaces another diagram is out of style.

Text rules: six or seven words per line at 14 px or larger, short lines, one
accent word at most. A number on screen is a fact, not a texture.

## 4. Chapters

A chapter is 3–5 beats and one numbered marker (`01 · Mở`, `02 · OpenCut
Reinforced`, …). The marker sits on the first line of the chapter, not on the
first frame of a scene.

* The marker label is what the viewer would call that section, not an internal
  beat id.
* A chapter lasts as long as its argument. In the reference, chapters run 7–50 s;
  the average is 25 s. Do not pad a chapter to hit a cadence.
* A chapter opens with a new viewpoint and closes by naming what it established.
* The last chapter is the end card: mark, one-line value, the honest licence
  line, one action.

## 5. Writing the narration

The voice is the film. Write it before the scenes.

* **One idea per line**, 25–45 words, 3.5–5.5 s spoken. If a line needs a comma
  splice to hold two ideas, it is two lines.
* **Name what is on screen at that moment.** "Đây là timeline" while a timeline
  assembles; not "công cụ mạnh mẽ" over a generic panel.
* **Concrete over adjectival.** "Cắt đúng khung" beats "chỉnh sửa chính xác".
* **Numbers are checked facts.** Version, date, platform, duration, price. If it
  was not verified in this session, it does not go on screen.
* **Honesty is a beat, not a disclaimer.** Say what is missing (mobile, notarisation,
  a paid provider) in its own chapter, in the same confident voice as the wins.
* **No feature lists.** A list is a beat that failed to become a transformation.
* **The close is one action.** "Mở dự án mẫu", "thử một cảnh" — not five links.

## 6. Reading rhythm

* Tempo **1.6** on the local TTS voice. 1.0 reads like an audiobook; above 1.8
  the consonants start to blur.
* **190 ms** between lines. That is a breath. A chapter change may take 400–600 ms,
  but the gap is written into the plan, not left to chance.
* **≈28 characters/second** at 1.6 on the reference voice. Measure it: speak one
  known line, divide characters by seconds, put the number in
  `narration.chars_per_second`. The fit check uses it to catch a line that lost
  words.
* A line that overruns the space before the next line is **rewritten shorter**,
  never sped up. `narration.mjs` reports the slack; a slack under 180 ms is a
  warning, not a style.
* Speech fills **90–96 %** of the runtime. The reference: 285.9 s spoken in
  300.0 s. Silence is reserved for a chapter turn or the final card, not sprinkled
  between lines.
* The film ends 1.4 s after the last measured line (or at an exact `duration_ms`).
  No trailing black.

## 7. Caption craft

* Captions are a **track**, never baked into a scene. The camera moves underneath
  a fixed subtitle.
* Timing comes from the measured audio: first chunk at the measured start, later
  chunks at their character position **+110 ms**, clamped to the next cue.
* Readability: **≤12 words, ≤72 characters, ≥900 ms** on screen. The reference
  averages 9 words and 1.4 s across 191 cues for 65 spoken lines.
* Never overlap the next cue; fold a two-word orphan into the previous card when
  it still fits.
* Look: Be Vietnam Pro, 25 pt, medium, bottom anchor, −280 basis points,
  `#F4F6FA` on `#0B0D11` at 120 alpha, 8000 milli-point padding. One layer, every
  cue styled.
* A caption that leads the voice by even half a second changes the feel of the
  film. Treat the +110 ms as a floor, not a target.

## 8. Music

* **120 bpm**, so every 0.5 s is a beat and every whole-second cut lands on the
  grid.
* **Constant −6 dB** under the voice for a documentary. `duckDb: null` is the
  house setting; per-sentence ducking is a showcase move, not a bed.
* Bake the level into the file (`ffmpeg -filter:a volume=-6dB`). Clip volume is
  app-only; the CLI has no gain verb.
* The bed runs the full film, including the gaps. It is a floor, not an event.
* One bed per film. A second music cue is a chapter decision, not a loop.

## 9. Assembly shape

The finished timeline is four tracks and a marker row:

| Track | Holds |
|---|---|
| video | one clip per beat, 0 → film length, no gaps |
| audio (voice) | one clip per line at its measured start |
| caption | every cue, one track, one style |
| audio (music) | one bed clip, 0 → film length |

Markers are rebuilt from the script, so the outline and the film never disagree.
Renders are files only; assembly is the one sequential pass that writes the
project. Review, then save once.

## 10. What "cinematic" is not

* Not a dark background with white text.
* Not a slow zoom on a still.
* Not a stack of glows standing in for depth.
* Not a feature list read aloud.
* Not a caption that arrives before the voice.
* Not a chapter that exists only to hold a marker.

# Style packs

Method-only packs for making a video look and sound like a proven one. A pack
carries timing, palette, camera, beat shape, cue rules and voice settings — never
narration text, names, claims or footage.

## Packs

| Pack | For | Path |
|---|---|---|
| Showcase | a one-minute product or feature film | `showcase/README.md` |
| Documentary | a multi-minute chaptered story | `../cinematic-story/STYLE.md` |

The documentary entry is the pre-existing cinematic style, kept in place until it
is split into the six-file shape.

## Contract

A pack is a directory with `README.md` and six method files: `motion.md`,
`story.md`, `script.md`, `voice.md`, `edit.md`, `captions.md`. Every number has a
unit and was measured on a real cut. If a rule only makes sense for one topic, it
belongs in that video's notes, not in a pack.

## Use

Read the pack README, then only the file the current decision needs. Keep the
canvas, frame rate and structural numbers; adapt speed and length to the
language and target duration. Write new content.

## Promote

When the user judges a video good and the approach is repeatable, copy
`showcase/` to `templates/styles/<slug>/`, replace the numbers with measured
ones, strip the content, add a row above and route the pack from `AGENTS.md`.
The full rule is in `../../docs/style-packs.md`.

# Captions

## Style

- 26 pt, anchored bottom, offset −420 px at 1080p.
- One style for the whole film: same size, anchor and offset on every cue.
- Two lines maximum; about 42 characters per line.
- Captions are clips on a caption track, never burned into a render.

## Timing

- 12–18 characters per second of reading speed.
- A cue lives 0.8–7 s. Split at punctuation, never mid-phrase.
- Start on the word, end a few frames after it; do not pad every cue to the
  same length.
- A cue never overlaps the next one.

## Wording

- Keep the speaker's words; fix only obvious recognition errors.
- Keep diacritics. Shorten the line instead of stripping marks.
- No speaker labels, no sound descriptions, no decorative punctuation.

## Check

Read the first, middle and last cue on the timeline. If a cue is clipped or
unreadable at normal speed, split it and re-import the SRT.

# Edit

## Rhythm

- Build the cut on the narration's beat grid, not on a music loop.
- Cut two frames before the word ends; the next image arrives on the syllable.
- One cut per beat minimum; a static shot longer than four seconds needs an
  internal move.
- No crossfades between beats. A hard cut is the style; a transition never runs
  longer than 200 ms.

## Gaps and holds

- 250 ms between spoken lines; let the last frame of a beat hold through it.
- Hold the final frame 300 ms after the last word before the music ends.
- Never cut mid-word and never leave a black frame between beats.

## Sound

- Music sits at −9 dB under speech; duck it, do not lower the whole mix.
- Music starts at frame zero and fades out over the last second.
- No sound effect on every cut; one accent per act at most.

## Check

Watch the first, middle and last ten seconds. If any cut lands on a breath or a
black frame, move it to the nearest word boundary.

# Motion

## Frame

- Canvas 1920×1080 at 30/1. One canvas for the whole film.
- A scene runs 4–8 s and carries one headline. Longer means split it.

## Palette

- Three to five flat fills: background, ink, one accent, one muted tone.
- Reuse the same fills across the film. No gradients, no stacked bands, no
  per-beat palette.
- Background is the darkest or lightest value; text never sits on the accent.

## Type

- Titles are 6–7 words per line, at least 28 px at 1080p, inside a 5 % margin.
- One type scale: headline, support, label. Do not add a fourth size.
- Let the renderer pick the face; write NFC text and keep diacritics.

## Camera and animation

- A slow push-in from zoom 1.0 to 1.08, or a pan of at most 32 px, keeps every
  frame alive. Keep zoom ≥ 1.
- Two or three animations run at once: drift, pulse, wipe. Entrance fades alone
  read as a slideshow.
- Entrance 300–500 ms, ease-out; exit 200–300 ms. Nothing snaps.
- No dead frame: at every second, something moves.

## Check

`tools/or motion layout --file SCENE --at 1/2 --json` — read the boxes, not a
screenshot. Text must stay inside the canvas and clear of the safe margin.

# Showcase pack

A one-minute product or feature film: motion-graphic beats over measured
narration, one music bed, real caption clips. This is the default style for a
complete short video; the machinery is
[`../../video-pipeline/README.md`](../../video-pipeline/README.md).

## Numbers

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Length | 55–75 s |
| Canvas | 1920×1080, 30/1 |
| Beats | 6–8 scenes, 4–8 s each |
| Narration | 17–20 characters/s, 180 wpm |
| Speech coverage | 45–60 % of the runtime |
| Gaps between lines | 250 ms |
| Captions | 26 pt, bottom, offset −420 px |
| Music | −9 dB under speech |

## Read in this order

1. `story.md` — the beat arc and what each beat must prove.
2. `script.md` — sentence length and the characters-per-second budget.
3. `motion.md` — palette, camera and animation density.
4. `voice.md` — rate, gaps and voice choice.
5. `edit.md` — cut rhythm and music level.
6. `captions.md` — cue length, size and position.

## Non-negotiables

- One idea per beat; a beat that needs two headlines is two beats.
- The first three seconds carry the hook; no logo-only opening.
- Every claim is visible on screen, not only spoken.
- The last beat lands the product identity and one next action.
- Captions are clips, never burned into a render.

# Script

## Budget

- 17–20 characters per second of Vietnamese narration at 180 wpm.
- One sentence per beat, 6–12 words.
- `duration_ms ≈ characters / 18 × 1000 + 250`; round up, never down.
- Speech covers 45–60 % of the beat; the rest is the image breathing.

## Shape

- Subject, verb, object. Concrete verbs: open, cut, render, speak.
- Numbers as they are spoken; no parentheses, no slash forms, no acronym soup.
- One name per thing; do not alternate between synonyms.
- The narration is what is said; the caption is the same meaning shortened to
  fit two lines. They may differ, but never contradict.

## Test

Read the line aloud once. If you stumble, the viewer will too; rewrite it
shorter. If a sentence needs a comma to survive, split it into two beats.

## Forbidden

Filler openings ("in today's world"), stacked adjectives, claims with no visible
proof, and sentences that describe the interface instead of the result.

# Story

## Arc

Seven beats, 55–75 s total:

1. **Hook** (3–5 s) — the outcome the viewer gets, stated as a fact.
2. **Problem** — the friction the product removes, shown in one image.
3. **Deconstruct** — the product opened up: the pieces the viewer will see.
4. **Core action** — the main editing or creation act, performed on screen.
5. **Assist** — the part a person could not do alone, with the result visible.
6. **Craft** — motion, voice or finish that proves quality, not a feature list.
7. **Close** — identity and one next action.

## Rules

- One idea per beat. If a beat needs two headlines, it is two beats.
- Every spoken claim has a visible proof in the same beat.
- The hook is not a logo, a title card or a greeting.
- The close is not a feature recap; it is the product name and one action.
- Speech covers 45–60 % of the runtime. Silence is punctuation, not a gap to
  fill.
- Beat order is fixed; beat length follows the narration, not the reverse.

# Voice

## Settings

- Rate 180 words per minute; 250 ms between lines.
- Voice order: the script's `voice`, then the app's saved default, then the
  first installed voice for the language. Never hardcode a voice name.
- One voice for the whole film; do not switch mid-piece.
- Mono 44.1 kHz WAV; the workspace voiceover tool writes this already.

## Delivery

- Short sentences carry emphasis; do not use capitals or punctuation tricks.
- Put the stressed word first or last in the sentence.
- Read the product name the same way every time.
- Leave the pause after a claim; do not fill it with a breath word.

## Before applying

Run the plan first and listen:

```sh
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/demo.json --plan --json
```

Fix wording until the read is clean, then run with `--apply`. A voiceover that
sounds rushed is a script problem, not a rate problem; shorten the line before
raising the speed.

# Review gates

Run these before rendering and again before saving. Each gate is a question, not
a checkbox you can tick by habit. The standard is the 59 s showcase, not "good
enough for a rough cut".

## 1. Frame gate — does every moment move?

Sample the beat at five times, including the middle.

* Is there at least one camera change and one secondary motion in *every* sample?
  A frame where only opacity is fading is a still frame — fail it.
* Is the beat a title card, a paragraph, or a diagram that replaces another
  diagram? Then it is not in the showcase style: rebuild it as a transformation.
* Does anything change form (a line becomes geometry, a clip becomes a layer, a
  code line becomes a shape), or does content merely appear and disappear?
* Does the shot hand off to the next one — a match cut, a dive, a fold, a wipe —
  rather than ending on an empty frame?

## 2. Composition gate

* Is all readable content above the caption band (`SAFE_BOTTOM` in `kit.mjs`)?
* Are there at most six or seven words in one line, at 14 px or larger?
* Does any shape or text leave its panel and sit over unrelated UI? (Rotated
  rectangles are the usual culprit.)
* Is the palette the same three-to-five flat colours as the rest of the film?
  Gradients, stacked bands that read as a gradient, and glow soup all fail.
* Does the camera ever expose the canvas edge? Keep zoom ≥ 0.94 except mid-dive.

## 3. Motion gate

* Does the camera move for the whole beat, not only at the cut?
* Do two elements interact — particles following a beam, a clip landing where the
  cursor pointed, a waveform and a caption tightening together?
* Is the beat's own idea visible in the first 0.8 s, before any text explains it?
* Does the motion read with the sound off? Mute the film and look again.

## 4. Sound gate

* Does each caption appear at or after the voice reaches that phrase?
* Does any line overrun the space before the next line? `narration.mjs` reports
  the slack; fix the wording rather than speeding the voice up.
* Is the bed a beat under every cut? 120 bpm at 0.5 s per beat is the default.
* Is the music −9 dB under the voice and still present in the gaps?
* Does the spoken audio fill 45–60 % of the runtime, with deliberate silence
  after the big moments?

## 5. Duration gate

* Does `build-scenes.mjs` report "windows tile exactly"?
* Does the video track run 0 → `duration_ms` with no gap and no overlap?
* Is the last frame the end of the last beat — no trailing black?
* Is the frame count `duration_ms / 1000 × fps` exactly (59 s × 30 fps = 1770)?
* If you exported, does the file report exactly `00:00:59.000` at its timebase?

## 6. Story and honesty gate

* If a beat were cut, would the viewer lose information, understanding or a
  memorable moment?
* Does the narration name what is on screen at that moment?
* Is every integration shown one the build actually supports? Do not show a
  harness, provider or model that is not in the app.
* Is a paid service described as paid, and a local/free path as local/free?
  Never imply paid services are free.
* Say which steps were verified in this session and which were not. Never claim
  the narration was listened to, or the export watched, if it was not.

# OR video pipeline — the showcase standard

A packaged workflow for building a **cinematic product film** from code: local
narration → a tiled beat plan → MotionScenes in the showcase style → parallel
render → one assembly pass into the open project. The reference is the 59-second
OpenCut Reinforced showcase: a finished shot breaks into its layers, the editor,
the assistant and the tools each get a designed beat, and the film closes on the
product.

This is the quality bar, not a slideshow generator. A beat that is a static title,
a paragraph of text or a diagram that only appears is **out of style**. Every
beat moves, transforms and hands off to the next one.

Nothing here changes the OR engine. It drives the app through `tools/or`, the
app's local TTS server and the deterministic MotionScene renderer.

## Contents

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `scripts/new-video.mjs` | Scaffold `videos/<slug>/` with `script.json` + `video.config.json` |
| `scripts/narration.mjs` | Local TTS → atempo → placed lines → measured manifest + caption cues |
| `scripts/build-scenes.mjs` | Beat windows → one MotionScene per beat (windows must tile the film) |
| `scripts/render.mjs` | Materialise every beat in parallel (files only, no project writes) |
| `scripts/assemble.mjs` | Tracks, narration, music, ducking, scenes, caption track, markers |
| `scripts/style-captions.mjs` | Re-apply the caption look after an SRT edit |
| `lib/kit.mjs` | Drawing kit: palette, primitives, camera presets, particles, waveforms |
| `lib/composers.mjs` | The eight showcase composers and the composer map |
| `lib/scenes/*.mjs` | The seven reference scenes, one file per beat |
| `beats/beat-library.json` | What each composer is for — pick by idea, not by habit |
| `CHECKLIST.md` | Image, motion, sync and honesty gates |
| `videos/example-showcase59/` | The 59 s showcase script and beat map |

## The five steps

Run from the workspace root (the folder with `project.json` and `tools/or`).
`$V` is the video folder; `$T` is this template's folder.

```sh
node $T/scripts/new-video.mjs --slug my-film --title "My film" --seconds 20

# 1. write the lines (start_ms per line) and the beat windows
$EDITOR videos/my-film/script.json videos/my-film/video.config.json

# 2. narration at 1.6×, placed at the planned times, with a fit check
node $T/scripts/narration.mjs --video videos/my-film --attach project.json

# 3. the bed: 120 bpm, so every whole-second cut lands on a beat
node tools/music.mjs --out work/music/bed.wav \
  --prompt "uplifting, 120 bpm, strong drums, 59 giây" --json

# 4. beats → scenes → rendered clips (3 workers is the sweet spot)
node $T/scripts/build-scenes.mjs --video videos/my-film
node $T/scripts/render.mjs --video videos/my-film --workers 3 --attach project.json

# 5. import everything into the open project, then review and save
node $T/scripts/assemble.mjs --video videos/my-film --attach project.json --dry-run
node $T/scripts/assemble.mjs --video videos/my-film --attach project.json
tools/or project save --attach project.json --json
```

`assemble.mjs` creates the tracks it needs, clears the ones it owns, imports the
SRT as a real caption track and styles every cue. `--dry-run` prints the plan
without touching the project.

## Config shape

```jsonc
{
  "slug": "my-film",
  "title": "My film",
  "tempo": 1.6,                       // narration time-stretch; 1.6 is the house tempo
  "duration_ms": 59000,               // exact film length; the windows must add up to this
  "canvas": { "width": 1920, "height": 1080 },
  "captions": { "anchor": "bottom", "sizePt": 26, "offsetY": -420, "weight": "medium" },
  "music": { "file": "work/music/bed.wav", "duckDb": -9 },
  "beats": [
    { "id": "open", "composer": "deconstruct", "start_ms": 0,     "end_ms": 5000,  "lines": ["mo"] },
    { "id": "ui",   "composer": "editor",      "start_ms": 5000,  "end_ms": 13000, "lines": ["ui", "ui2"] },
    { "id": "close","composer": "close",       "start_ms": 52000, "end_ms": 59000, "lines": ["ket"] }
  ]
}
```

* `start_ms`/`end_ms` are the beat window. Windows must start at 0, touch each
  other and end at `duration_ms`; `build-scenes.mjs` refuses anything else and
  refuses a narration line no beat owns. For a long explainer you may drop
  `end_ms` and let a beat run to the next beat's first line.
* `lines` are `script.json` ids. A line's `start_ms` is where its voice sits, so
  keep it inside its beat and leave at least 180 ms before the next line.
* `composer` is a key in `beats/beat-library.json`.
* Composers take 5–13 s. A five-minute film is 25–35 beats, not five long ones.

## The showcase arc

The 59 s reference, which is the default shape for a product intro:

| Window | Composer | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| 0–5 s | `deconstruct` | A finished shot holds the frame, then breaks into picture / sound / voice / captions and folds into a line |
| 5–13 s | `editor` | The editor builds itself, clips drop in, the playhead sweeps, the camera dives into the viewer |
| 13–22 s | `assistant` | A request leaves the chat, an MCP beam reaches external harnesses, a clip comes home |
| 22–31 s | `motionScene` | Code lines turn into geometry that assembles a shot, then the camera enters it |
| 31–39 s | `voiceWhisper` | The script is spoken, the waveform fills, Whisper returns synced captions |
| 39–52 s | `assembly` | Four lanes converge, gaps close, the camera dives into the programme monitor and the finished film plays |
| 52–59 s | `close` | Mark and wordmark, what it is, the honest licence line, one call to action |

Vary the viewpoint between beats: wide shot, user view, close-up, inside-view,
comparison. Two UI beats in a row is a fail even if both are polished.

## Timing budget

* This voice at tempo 1.6 speaks about **17–20 characters per second**. Measure,
  never estimate: `narration.mjs` prints each line's real duration and its slack.
* Spoken audio should fill **45–60 %** of the runtime. A 59 s film carries
  25–30 s of speech; the rest is music and picture. Do not pad with empty scenes
  and do not speed the voice up to hit a length.
* Silence is a tool: leave 0.8–2 s after a big visual moment.
* The film ends on the last frame of the last beat, not on a trailing black gap.
* Music at 120 bpm puts a beat every 0.5 s, so any whole-second cut lands on the
  grid. Duck the bed −9 dB under the voice.

## Rules the template enforces

* **The windows tile the film.** Every beat is a non-empty window, the first
  starts at 0, each starts where the previous ended, the last ends at
  `duration_ms`. The sum of rendered frames is the film length, exactly.
* **Captions are a track, not baked.** A scene camera moves underneath a fixed
  subtitle. `assemble.mjs` imports the SRT and runs `timeline set-text` on every
  cue (bottom anchor, 26 pt, −420 offset).
* **Captions never lead the voice.** The first chunk of a line starts at the
  measured audio start; later chunks start at their character position + 110 ms,
  clamped to the next cue.
* **No line can lose words.** A line that comes back under 80 % of the duration
  its text implies is re-spoken sentence by sentence and stitched.
* **Renders are revision-safe.** `render.mjs` only writes files; every project
  write happens later, sequentially, in `assemble.mjs`.
* **Every frame moves.** Composers animate a camera over the whole beat and keep
  two or three secondary motions running. There is no still frame.

## Pitfalls that cost time

* A media item caches the duration it was imported with. Re-rendering a file in
  place keeps the old length; remove the media item (or re-insert the clip) when
  a render's length changes.
* `insert-clip --duration` must not exceed the media duration. A 1.181875 s WAV
  refuses `--duration 1.182`; floor to milliseconds.
* Keep rationals reduced (`591/500`, not `1182000/1000000`) and times exact.
* Node ids are unique across a whole scene. Prefix every piece (`imSun`,
  `auWave`, `c1`) — a duplicate id fails validation, not just review.
* Scene text is laid out with a 5 % margin inside the remaining box; `kit.mjs`
  converts ink coordinates for you. Keep type at 14 px or larger and lines short.
* Camera zoom stays at 0.94–1.5 except for a deliberate dive; the backdrop is
  oversized so a zoom never shows the canvas edge.
* Editing the project while renders are running causes revision conflicts —
  render and assemble are separate steps for that reason.
* Three parallel workers is the sweet spot; more workers mostly add contention.

## A worked example

`videos/example-showcase59/` is the reference film: 19 narration lines, 7 beats,
59.000 s, 30 fps. It expects `work/music/bed.wav` (generate it with step 3) and
runs the five steps unchanged. Read its `video.config.json` first; it is the
clearest statement of the standard.

## Provenance

Built from the 59 s OpenCut Reinforced showcase assembled in the OR workspace:
seven hand-authored MotionScene beats, 1770 frames at 30 fps, VieNeu-TTS at 1.6,
a 120 bpm bed, and a real caption track. The kit and the seven scene modules are
those scenes with the project-specific narration removed.

# Workspace tools

Scope: the local commands this workspace exposes. `tools/or` is the default way
to read and change the open project; `mcp__or__*` tools are the fallback for
motion insertion, the motion library, and a CLI failure. Some operations belong to
the app alone — speed, volume, group move, effects, export, recording, cloud
voices — and have no verb here on purpose. Title and caption styling does have a
verb: `timeline set-text`.

| Command | Use |
|---|---|
| `tools/or <verb> --attach project.json --json` | The OR CLI bound to the running app build. Reads and edits the live project through the app-written pointer. `tools/or commands` and `tools/or queries` list the verbs. |
| `tools/or media clean-audio --source IN --out OUT` | Offline noise reduction; writes a new file that you import to use. |
| `tools/or captions transcribe` | Transcribe one media item locally (Vietnamese/English auto-detected); needs the running app. |
| `tools/or timeline import-captions` | Apply a reviewed SRT/WebVTT file as a new caption track. |
| `tools/or motion ...` | Validate, inspect, evaluate, layout, render, from-code, materialize or publish a scene. `publish` saves it to the library, renders, imports **and** inserts in one call. |
| `tools/or motion asset ...` | List, validate, save, instantiate, import, remove or insert from the app's motion library; pass `--attach project.json` and the CLI resolves the folder from the pointer. |
| `node tools/motion-scaffold.mjs` | Write a valid V1 `.ormotion.json` skeleton into `scenes/`. |
| `node tools/voiceover.mjs` | Speak an `or-assistant-script` with the macOS voice, write exact timings and SRT, optionally import and place the result. |
| `node tools/music.mjs` | Synthesise a quiet, royalty-free background music bed offline, from a prompt or explicit flags. |

The app keeps its motion library at `<application support>/motion-library`, and the
workspace `project.json` records that path, so every motion verb resolves it from
`--attach project.json`. `--library PATH` overrides it for one call.

## Examples

```sh
tools/or project summary --attach project.json --json
tools/or timeline tracks --attach project.json --json
tools/or timeline clips --track TRACK_ID --attach project.json --json
tools/or timeline markers --attach project.json --json
tools/or media list --attach project.json --json
tools/or media clean-audio --source /absolute/in.wav --out /absolute/out.wav --json
tools/or project save --attach project.json --json
tools/or motion validate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion inspect --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion evaluate --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --json
tools/or motion layout --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --json
tools/or motion from-code --source work/sample.rs --output scenes/sample.ormotion.json
tools/or motion render --file scenes/title.ormotion.json --at 1/2 --output work/title.png
tools/or motion publish --attach project.json --scene scenes/title.ormotion.json --json
tools/or motion asset list --attach project.json --json
tools/or motion asset insert --attach project.json --asset-id ASSET_ID --json
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/demo.json --plan --json
node tools/voiceover.mjs --script work/scripts/demo.json --out work/voiceover/demo --apply --attach project.json --json
node tools/music.mjs --out work/music/bed.wav --prompt "nhạc nền nhẹ nhàng 30 giây, không trống" --json
tools/or captions transcribe --attach project.json --media MEDIA_ID --srt-out work/captions/clip.srt --json
tools/or timeline import-captions --attach project.json --file work/captions/clip.srt --json
```

`motion publish` needs the running app: it validates the scene, saves it as a
reusable library asset, renders it, imports the video and inserts an ordinary clip
through validated commands. Pass `--no-library` to skip the asset save on purpose.
`motion materialize` only writes a file; use it when a file is the goal, not as an
insertion path. The MCP motion tools are a fallback for a CLI failure, not the
default.

## Bounds

- `tools/or` is written by the app on connect; editing it is pointless.
- Scaffold and CLI write only the files you name; nothing else is project state.
- No workspace tool reads a cloud key. Narration keys live in the macOS keychain
  and belong to the app's Settings → Narration panel.
